status: APPROVED by the operator 11/19 evening ("Approve"); skeptic review before any code runs
registered: 2026-11-19 evening ET, before any grid cell was built or any outcome computed
operator: 11/19 'I want to run a loop simulation of an A/B test - gathering the best performing setup for our opening' -> 'Yes, draft the grid and holdout rule'
question: Of a fixed grid of opening setups (signal x window x name filter), which is best after real spreads, and is the best one good enough to beat what a search over random entries finds by luck?
universe: warehouse SIP top-400 by prior-day dollar volume, ETFs/ETPs excluded (board_structure_family.universe); price $20-$400 at the trigger bar (the live band)
entry: trigger read at the CLOSE of 1-minute bar t; buy at the OPEN of bar t+1; one entry per (cell, name, day) - the first trigger in the window
cost: real SIP quoted spread in the 60 s before entry (news_source.fetch_quotes, shared cache); spread > 15 bp not traded; net = gross - spread
exit (primary, every cell): the desk bracket (holistic_entry.bracket: +20 bp before -50 bp within 15 min, stop first on a two-touch minute)

signal.SQUARE: fast %R (21, EWM 7) and slow %R (112, EWM 3) both >= -20 on bar t and not on t-1, fast rising (opening_square.square_bars) - 'extended past entry'
signal.ORB: first 1-minute close above the high of the 09:30-09:34 bars (5-minute opening range breakout); no trigger before 09:35
signal.HEAT20: heat = 100 + fast %R < 20, rising on t and t-1, not t-2 (low_heat_rising.heat_turns with the heat < 20 cut)

name filter (at the trigger bar, live va.F1: day change +1.5% to +4%, any volume pace
name filter (at the trigger bar, live va.F2: day change +1.5% to +4%, volume pace >= 1.5 (cumulative volume / prior-day volume / elapsed session share)

the loop (one refinement round, capped): ROUND 1 scores all 48 cells on SEARCH. ROUND 2 takes the top 3 cells by mean net and scores up to 8 neighbors each (window edges shifted +/-5 min; day-change edge 4% moved to 3% / 6%; pace cut 1.5 moved to 1.0 / 2.0), at most 24 new cells. No further rounds. Every cell from both rounds counts in the multiple-testing penalty (at most 72).

HOLDOUT RULE.search: 2026-04-28 .. 2026-09-23 only. All ranking, refining and choosing happens here.
HOLDOUT RULE.confirm: 2026-09-24 .. 2026-11-18, opened ONCE, for the single chosen cell (runner-up reported as information only). The confirm data are not read for any cell before the choice is written to this file with a timestamp.
HOLDOUT RULE.forward: the next 10 live sessions after the choice, replayed through replay_session.py with the cell's rule and the real recorded spreads - a holdout nobody has seen, because 9/24-11/18 has been used by earlier studies
HOLDOUT RULE.disclosed overlap: tonight's opening_square study already scores SQUARE in 09:30-09:58 on the confirm period; that result will be seen before this grid runs. It is reported next to the grid, and SQUARE cells are not exempted from any bar.

choice (on SEARCH): the cell with the highest mean net bp per trade among cells with >= 150 traded entries; ties by $/day on a 3-slot $3,200 book

pass (all required).search_penalty: day-clustered t >= 3.3 on SEARCH (Bonferroni over up to 72 cells, alpha 0.05)
pass (all required).beats_luck: mean net on SEARCH above the 95th percentile of the BEST cell in 200 random-entry grids (each random grid replaces the signal with a random minute in the same window, on the same name-days that pass the same filter; same exit; gross minus that cell's median quoted spread, so no extra quotes are needed)
pass (all required).edge: mean net >= +2.0 bp per trade on SEARCH
pass (all required).both_halves: mean net > 0 in both date halves of SEARCH
pass (all required).confirm: mean net > 0 and day-clustered t >= 1.5 on CONFIRM
pass (all required).forward: mean net > 0 over the 10 forward sessions

reported for every cell (information): trades, opens per day, win %, mean net bp, $/day and max drawdown on the 3-slot book, median hold, median spread and share removed by the gate, lift vs the same cell's random-entry control
sample and cost control: <= 400 traded entries per cell on SEARCH, chosen by the lowest sha256('ogrid'|day|sym|t); quotes shared across cells and with earlier studies' cache; quote fetching only after 16:05 ET and after tonight's study chains finish (the data key is shared with the live dashboard)
if_pass: result-skeptic review, then the chosen cell as a default-off arm for its window only, replayed through the live code, then paper
if_fail: record which cells came closest and that the best of the grid does not beat a search over random entries; the opening is not where the money is with these signals and the desk bracket
pre_run_review: result-skeptic reviews this prereg before any code runs (standing checkpoint)
